system.name: Canvas
system.one_liner: isolates and adaptively swaps remote memory for multiple co-located applications

content.subject: how a page fault is handled: swap-cache lookup, memory accounting, optional eviction, and fetch, ending in a PTE update

elements.name: Begin
elements.role: start of handling one page fault

elements.name: Lookup Swap Cache
elements.role: checks whether the faulting page is already cached locally; lock-protected

elements.name: cgroup Accounting
elements.role: checks whether there is enough local physical memory to swap in the page

elements.name: Swap Out (Entry Alloc)
elements.role: makes room and allocates a swap entry when local memory is insufficient; lock-protected

elements.name: Prefetching
elements.role: speculatively fetches additional pages predicted from recent swap history

elements.name: RDMA Read
elements.role: issues the RDMA read that fetches the faulting page from remote memory

elements.name: Update Metadata
elements.role: records the newly available page's metadata

elements.name: Set PTE
elements.role: installs the page table entry so the faulting access can proceed

elements.name: End
elements.role: handling of the page fault completes

elements.name: Use locks to serialize concurrent executions.

content.key_idea: A page fault takes one of three shortcuts depending on cache and memory state, but every path converges on the same metadata-update and PTE-install finish, with only two steps needing locks.

evidence: Figure 1 illustrates the kernel's remote access data path where remote memory is mapped into the host server
If a page can be found there, it gets mapped to a virtual page and removed from the swap cache
If there is, the kernel issues an RDMA read request, which is then pushed into RDMA's dispatch queue.

summary: This figure is a flowchart of the kernel's remote-access data path in Canvas, tracing how one page fault is handled from Begin to End. The kernel first looks up the swap cache: on a Hit the page is already available, so the flow jumps straight to updating metadata; on a Miss it proceeds to cgroup accounting, which checks whether local memory is sufficient. If there is enough local memory, the kernel goes directly to prefetching and issuing an RDMA read; otherwise it first performs Swap Out (Entry Alloc) to make room and allocate a swap entry before the same prefetching and RDMA read steps. Both paths converge at Update Metadata, then Set PTE, then End. A pink fill and padlock icon mark the two steps, Lookup Swap Cache and Swap Out (Entry Alloc), that must be serialized with locks against concurrent page faults.
summary_zh: 该图是Canvas内核远程访问数据路径流程图：缺页缓存命中则直接更新元数据；未命中经cgroup记账，内存充足则直接预取+RDMA读，否则先Swap Out分配条目再读取；两条路径汇合后更新元数据、设置PTE；粉色和锁标记需加锁两步。
notes: base set to 'flowchart' rather than the prior label's 'component' since the figure uses standard flowchart iconography (oval begin/end, diamond decisions, boxed steps); groups kept as ['logic'] since the guard labels (Hit/Miss/Otherwise/Enough local memory) carry no numbered or lettered markers, so 'walkthrough' does not apply. The arrow routing was traced directly from the high-resolution source image: the 'Enough local memory' branch and the 'Swap Out (Entry Alloc)' branch both merge into the same pair of arrows feeding 'Prefetching' and 'RDMA Read', while only the 'Hit' branch bypasses all the way to 'Update Metadata' -- this matches the paragraph's description.
